chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from one who narrated to him, from Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him) who said:
'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Supplication after the affliction has descended does not benefit.'

key_terms.الدُّعَاء: Supplication, du'a — an earnest prayer or invocation addressed to God
key_terms.الْبَلَاء: Trial, affliction, tribulation — divine test or calamity that befalls a person
key_terms.يُنْتَفَعُ: To benefit, to derive advantage — passive form indicating that benefit is not obtained

ai.seo_question: Is supplication (du'a) effective after an affliction has already descended?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) reports that Imam Zayn al-'Abidin (peace be upon him) used to teach that du'a (supplication) is only truly beneficial when made before a trial or affliction descends — not after it has already fallen upon a person. This teaching emphasizes the importance of proactive, preventive supplication as a spiritual shield. In the early Islamic tradition, du'a was understood not merely as a petition in times of crisis, but as an ongoing act of worship and a form of connection with God that must be cultivated before difficulties arise.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said:
‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘One cannot benefit from a supplication after the descent of the affliction’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Washsha’ from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from abu al-Hassan al-Awwal (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) would say, ‘Prayer and pleading before Allah for help after the fall of misfortune does not benefit one.’”
